title: 3-Read Friday #21: PISA Results, ChatGPT's Origins, and Mobile Phone Bans
author: Craig Barton
summary: In the 21st issue of 3-Read Friday, Craig Barton curates three posts responding to end-of-2023 education-technology and data anxieties. He opens with Alex Quigley's digest of the newly released PISA 2022 results, valuing it as a way to process a confusing wave of national comparison data through nine distilled reflections rather than raw headlines. His second pick, Dan Meyer's "Happy 60th Birthday, ChatGPT," extends generative AI's hype cycle back sixty years by comparing 1960s predictions about teaching machines to today's claims about AI tutors, which Barton flags as food for thought rather than endorsement. His third selection, from the InnerDrive team, draws a policy parallel between historical UK smoking bans and the then-emerging case for banning mobile phones in schools, arguing environmental restriction succeeds where awareness campaigns alone stall. Barton's own framing across all three - brief, non-committal, letting each writer's argument stand largely on its own - is typical of the format: less a personal thesis than a curated reading list for a busy teaching audience heading into a weekend. The issue closes, as usual, with a pointer to his newsletter archive and a sign-off wishing readers a good weekend.
points: Barton foregrounds Alex Quigley's PISA 2022 rundown as an antidote to headline overload, pointing readers to a condensed nine-point summary rather than the raw data dump.
He frames Dan Meyer's Happy 60th Birthday, ChatGPT as a check on generative-AI hype, noting Meyer's century-spanning parallel between 1960s teaching-machine predictions and today's AI-tutor claims.
Barton closes with a practical policy angle, using InnerDrive's smoking-ban analogy to argue that a UK schools phone ban needs environmental change alongside education, not education alone.

Across all three picks, Barton's own editorial thread is skepticism toward technology-as-panacea narratives in education, whether about AI transforming teaching or unmanaged data driving national panic.
quotes: With the 2022 PISA results released this week, there is information aplenty about which countries have risen and fallen, in which subjects, along with speculation as to why. It’s easy to get overwhelmed. Fortunately, Alex has written a lovely summary, picking out 9 key points to reflect upon.

Dan shares predictions people were making about the role technology would play in transforming education in the 1960s, and compares these with the predictions people are currently making about the role of generative AI. Lots of food for thought.

There has been a lot of talk about banning mobile phones in schools recently, with advocates speculating that our future selves will look back upon this time and wonder how these attention-sapping devices were ever allowed in our schools.
Here, the Inner Drive team draw parallels between the smoking ban to help schools enforce a policy that is bound to be met with resistance.
If you found this edition of 3-Read Friday useful, feel free to share it with colleagues.
